item.title: 1.0.0-beta.11
item.description:
AI agents act faster and see more, with you able to take over at any moment; Linux VMs are ready in minutes; the library and the new-VM sheet are rebuilt; the clipboard keeps formatting and carries files both ways; and Windows VMs get a microphone.
### Added - `vm_actions`: up to 50 keys, typing, clicks, drags, scrolls and waits in one call, each decided and audited as its own request, and every input tool says whether the screen changed (`verified`, with where). `vm_power start` can wait for the guest tools. - `vm_read_screen`: the text on any guest's screen (recognised on the Mac), and its controls on Windows (UI Automation) and macOS (Accessibility), to click by id; marked as the guest's text, never instructions. - `vm_exec` with `desktop` opens an app on the signed-in user's desktop (all three guests); `vm_sign_in` signs a locked guest in with a password VMPane keeps and types itself, never shown to the agent (off per VM; at Run commands and Full control you are asked first). - Linux VMs from Ubuntu 26.04, Debian 13 and Fedora 44 cloud images: nothing to click through, guest tools and SSH (on 127.0.0.1) ready on the first boot, with an optional GNOME desktop. - The VM's window shows an AI agent at work: who, at what level, what it just did, with **Take Over** and **Stop**. Typing or clicking in the VM while an agent acts takes over too; agents wait (`takenOver`) until you resume. Agents' questions appear in the VM's window. - A new library, in the style of macOS 26 (and Sequoia's on macOS 15): filters with their counts in the sidebar, the VMs as a list or a grid with each system's own tile, and an inspector with the chosen VM's actions, its problem and fix, and its system, resources (a stopped VM's processors, memory, display and disk change without starting it), snapshots and agent activity. - New VM is one sheet: the systems listed by kind (macOS, Linux, Windows, an installer file from this Mac) and the chosen one's detail, sized for your Mac (⌘N, then Return makes another of the last one), made in the background with each stage in the library. Drop an .iso or .ipsw on the library or the Dock icon to start from it. A Linux VM made from the sheet gets a password VMPane keeps for you (**Copy Password** in the inspector). - A VM's settings are sections in a sidebar, as in System Settings (General, Hardware, Display, Sharing, AI agents, Network, Port Forwarding); the agents' levels are a list that says what each allows. - The clipboard of macOS and Windows VMs keeps formatting: bold, links, colours, fonts and tables copied in Word, Outlook, Excel or a browser paste formatted on the other side (HTML and RTF, with plain text alongside; **Keep text formatting** in Settings › Sharing turns it off) (#6). - Files and folders copy and paste both ways: ⌘C in Finder, Ctrl-V in Explorer pastes them into the open folder, and files copied in the VM paste where you press ⌘V in Finder (up to 1000 files and 2 GB a copy) (#6). - Files dragged out of a Windows VM's window drop in Finder, copied from the VM; nothing moves in Windows (#6).
### Changed - Files copied in a VM no longer land in `~/Downloads/VMPane/<VM>`: they wait in a staging folder until pasted, and the next copy replaces them. - Downloads can be cancelled and resume later; a VM appears in the library only once its downloads are done, so a quit midway leaves none behind. - Keys or mouse buttons an agent left held down are let go when you take over or the agent leaves.
### Fixed - Windows VMs had no microphone: QEMU's CoreAudio backend only plays sound, so Windows got a speaker and nothing to record from. Their sound now goes over SPICE to the VM's own window process, which plays it and, with Microphone on, gives Windows a microphone fed by the Mac's; QEMU no longer reaches the Mac's audio at all (#7). macOS asks once whether "VMPane VM" may use the microphone, the first time Windows records. A Windows VM suspended or snapshotted before this version with Microphone on may show its microphone only after Windows restarts. - Cancelling a Parallels import or a cloud-image create just before its conversion started could crash VMPane.
### Not checked before this release - `agent-hud`: https://github.com/nhtera/vmpane/issues/10 - `mcp-actions`: https://github.com/nhtera/vmpane/issues/11

item.title: 1.0.0-beta.10
item.description:
Windows VMs on the shared network resolve names, and Windows VMs share the clipboard.
### Added - Windows VMs share the clipboard through VMPane's guest agent: text and images both ways, and files copied in the VM arrive in `~/Downloads/VMPane/<VM>`. Existing VMs get it by updating the guest tools (#5).
### Fixed - A Windows VM on the shared (NAT) network could not resolve names: QEMU's sandbox kept it from reading the Mac's DNS servers, so the network's DNS (10.0.2.3) never answered. The same sandbox rule filled `qemu.log` with thousands of "Conversion from character set" lines (#5).

item.title: 1.0.0-beta.9
item.description:
VMPane warns when the Mac is low on memory for a VM.
### Added - VMPane asks before starting a VM that can use more memory than the Mac has available (Cancel or Start Anyway), and a running VM's window warns while the Mac is almost out of memory. `vmpane start` prints the same warning. On a Mac out of memory, Linux VMs crashed or froze with memory that changed under them (e.g. a Debian install stuck at "Scanning the mirror"); the same VMs ran cleanly once memory was free.

item.title: 1.0.0-beta.8
item.description:
The new-VM wizard starts with macOS chosen, and a VM closed during a Windows install stays as it was left.
### Changed - The new-VM wizard opens with macOS chosen, so Continue works at once; click Linux or Windows 11 to change it.
### Fixed - A VM's process that shut down during an automatic Windows install could still write the install's progress or the VM's settings after letting go of the VM, and start the VM again if the install had just finished. It now finishes that work first and leaves the VM off; the next start continues from there.

item.title: 1.0.0-beta.7
item.description:
A Linux VM's text keeps its size when its resolution changes while it runs.
### Fixed - A resolution changed in a running Linux VM's settings reached the VM in pixels, not in points as at its start, so at Standard scaling a desktop or installer (e.g. Debian's) redrew its text at half its size until the VM restarted or its window was resized.

item.title: 1.0.0-beta.6
item.description:
The new-VM wizard no longer looks as if macOS were chosen.
### Fixed - With keyboard navigation on, the new-VM wizard opened with a focus ring on the macOS card that looked like a choice, and the ring stayed there after a click on another system. Focus now follows the chosen system, and the chosen card shows one border, not two.

item.title: 1.0.0-beta.5
item.description:
A Linux VM's boot menu is readable too.
### Fixed - A Linux VM's boot menu (GRUB) and first boot messages are readable: VMPane shows the top-left corner of the VM firmware's 8192 × 4320 boot screen at one guest pixel per point until Linux sets the VM's own size. - An AI agent's file transfer or command cut by the kill switch ends with a result the agent can read, not a protocol error, when the switch closes its connection before the transfer's own answer arrives. - The kill switch stops an agent's command that was still waiting (for the person's answer, the session's undo snapshot or the VM to start it), also when the app lets agents act again before the wait ends.

item.title: 1.0.0-beta.4
item.description:
A Linux VM's boot and installer are readable from the start.
### Fixed - A Linux VM with Larger scaling starts at its size in points, so its boot messages and installer are readable from the start (only the boot loader's own menu, e.g. GRUB, still picks the largest screen and shows small).

item.title: 1.0.0-beta.3
item.description:
A readable Linux display, a menu bar and clean Quit for each VM, and an install guide in the disk image.
### Changed - VoiceOver finds a VM's screen (named after the VM), and the settings' "Live" and "Next start" badges are easier to read. - A new Linux VM gets one pixel per point of its window, so the installer and consoles are readable on a Retina screen (they were half size). Settings → Display → Scaling now applies to Linux VMs too. - The disk image shows how to install: VMPane beside the Applications folder, with an arrow to drag it there.
### Fixed - A VM's own app ("VMPane VM") has a menu bar: Quit, Hide, Edit and Window (⌘ keys typed into the VM's screen still go to the VM). Quitting it, also from its Dock tile, asks first while the VM runs and then shuts the VM down cleanly; before, it had no menu and a Quit from the Dock ended a running VM at once.

item.title: 1.0.0-beta.2
item.description:
Fixes for the first beta.
### Fixed - Deleting or cloning a VM that was shut down from its own window works: VMPane first quits the VM's process, which stays open after the VM stops (1.0.0-beta.1 refused with "VMRunning()"). - A Windows VM's guest agent comes back at once after the VM resumes from a suspend or a live snapshot is restored, without a Windows restart (works with the 1.0.0-beta.1 agent too). - The VMPane folder in Application Support is private (0700) again: 1.0.0-beta.1 could make it readable by other accounts on the Mac (the files in it were already private). `vmpane doctor` reported it.

item.title: 1.0.0-beta.1
item.description:
The first public beta.
### Added - macOS and Linux guests on Virtualization.framework: install macOS from an Apple restore image (IPSW) and Linux from an ISO; suspend and resume; live and offline snapshots. - Windows 11 ARM guests on QEMU with Hypervisor.framework, a software TPM and Secure Boot; an unattended install from your own ISO that resumes after an interruption. - The VMPane guest agent for Linux, macOS and Windows: shared clipboard, drag and drop of files, file transfer and commands. - Shared folders and port forwarding. - Import of Parallels Desktop VMs. - The `vmpane` command-line tool and a built-in MCP server (`vmpane mcp`): AI coding agents drive only the VMs you open to them, at the level you choose (every VM starts at Off), and the kill switch stops them all. - Updates through Sparkle; VMPane asks before installing one, and running VMs keep running.
